transcript.text: Hello everyone. Before we finalize the interview panel for the team-lead role, I'd like to go through our standard pre-selection check. As a reminder, Mara and Jonah are our two internal finalists. I need to appoint a three-person panel from the available panelists — Elliot, Rina, Sofia, and Tariq — and the panel will evaluate both candidates against the same leadership criteria and provide a written recommendation. As part of our routine process, I'm asking the hiring manager, a peer manager, HR, and our employee representative to raise any relevant process or relationship considerations I should be aware of before we proceed. Does anyone have anything to flag?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a potential conflict of interest: Rina is Jonah's close personal friend and has been coaching him informally for the past year. I should have put this in the selection file earlier, but I was expecting Helena to ask about panel conflicts before any appointments were made. I'm disclosing this now so it can be factored into the panel composition.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thanks, Helena. As peer manager, I don't have any relationship or process concerns to flag regarding the panel composition. I would note, though, that I'm aware Elliot has had multiple firsthand observations of Mara coaching team members through difficult disagreements — four specific instances — that have not yet been formally entered into the leadership-evidence record. I think that's something we should be aware of as we proceed, and I can work on getting those documented properly. I'll defer to others for their considerations as well.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: As HR, I need to flag a process gap: I confirmed this week that our internal-selection procedure requires a standardized question set and an individual written score sheet from every panelist. The current selection packet does not yet state either requirement, so we'll need to update it before the panel proceeds to ensure compliance.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: As employee representative, I need to raise an accessibility consideration on behalf of Mara. Mara has informed me she has a documented accessibility need requiring two accommodations: first, she must receive the interview questions at least 48 hours in advance, and second, she must be permitted to submit written responses rather than answering any questions verbally. She asked me to raise this during process planning. I understand this hasn't been surfaced to Helena yet, so I'm formally disclosing it now so it can be incorporated into the assessment design. I'd also note that our accessibility practice requires that once a candidate states accessibility needs through the employee representative, those needs must be implemented — and that equal treatment means equivalent opportunity to demonstrate the criteria, even when the interview format differs between candidates.
transcript.speaker: A5
